briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Fights, Trials, and Takeovers: Michigan Holds Steady as National Cannabis Momentum Builds
briefs.top: Michigan operators are proving the 24% wholesale tax hasn't broken the market — new stores are opening in Washtenaw County, licensed demand is holding, and a gubernatorial front-runner is campaigning on repeal. Nationally, the industry kept pushing forward this week with a new DEA Schedule III registration portal, fresh M&A from Curaleaf and Spherex, and Compass Pathways planting its flag with a first U.S. office.

local.text: Bloom City Club opens Ypsilanti storefront — Ann Arbor's Bloom City Club is celebrating its new Ypsilanti dispensary with cannabis-themed events running through October.

Licensed demand holds steady despite new tax — Michigan's feared price spike and demand collapse under the 24% wholesale tax hasn't materialized two months into 2026, with the state's licensed market still far outselling the illicit trade compared to California.
GOP nominee John James vows to repeal wholesale tax — James has made repealing or reducing Michigan's 24% cannabis wholesale tax part of his gubernatorial platform heading into the November election.

Second tax lawsuit clears first hurdle, heads to trial — A Court of Claims judge declined to block the wholesale tax at the preliminary stage, but MiCIA's constitutional challenge over 'tax pyramiding' is now headed toward a full trial.

State regulators clean house, leveling the field — The CRA revoked 20 cultivation licenses and fined a grower $2 million for shipping 'dirt and mulch,' while also pulling Muha Meds' Ypsilanti dispensary license over a fake customer profile scheme.

national.text: DEA opens new Schedule III registration portal — The agency's Diversion Control Division launched a fresh Form 225 application process so state-licensed medical cannabis manufacturers, distributors and labs can register under the Controlled Substances Act.
Curaleaf sweetens Aurora Cannabis takeover bid — Curaleaf raised its offer by 25% to $5 per share, an 86% premium to Aurora's unaffected share price, in its bid for the Canadian cannabis giant.

Spherex buys two Colorado grows, nearly doubles staff — Colorado's top cannabis brand is acquiring cultivation facilities from The Cannabist Company in its first-ever acquisition, adding roughly 60 employees and going vertically integrated.

Compass Pathways opens its first U.S. office — The psilocybin biotech cut the ribbon on a Jersey City office with local elected officials as its COMP360 treatment keeps its FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation.

Rescheduling paused, not dead, DEA judge clarifies — A chief administrative law judge stayed the Schedule III marijuana case to weigh a new GAO report, with the government's response due October 13 and the path to Schedule III still open.
